chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) led the people in Dhuhr and Asr prayers when the sun began to decline, in congregation, without any reason; and he led them in Maghrib and the last Isha prayer before the disappearance of the twilight, without any reason, in congregation. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) did this only so that the time might be expanded for his community.

key_terms.الظهر والعصر: Dhuhr and Asr — the midday and afternoon prayers, combined at the time of Dhuhr
key_terms.المغرب والعشاء: Maghrib and Isha — the sunset and night prayers, combined at Maghrib time
key_terms.سقوط الشفق: Disappearance of the twilight — the end of Maghrib's preferred window
key_terms.في جماعة: In congregation — emphasizing this was a communal act, not done privately
key_terms.ليتسع الوقت: So that the time may be expanded — the Prophet's explicit reason for combining
key_terms.من غير علة: Without a reason/excuse — meaning no illness, travel, rain, or other jurisprudential excuse

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet combine Dhuhr and Asr prayers without an excuse?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) deliberately combined Dhuhr with Asr, and Maghrib with Isha, in congregation, without any travel or illness as justification. This hadith establishes the permissibility of combining prayers (jam' al-salatayn) even without an excuse, as the Prophet's intent was to give his community flexibility in timing. This narration is foundational in Shia fiqh, where combining prayers at their earliest prescribed times is a widespread and accepted practice.
word_analysis: so that it may be expanded
